name: Progress OpenEdge
tagline: Integrated RDBMS plus ABL 4GL application platform behind thousands of ERP and vertical business apps.
description: OpenEdge is Progress Software's application platform: a transactional relational database tightly coupled to ABL (formerly Progress 4GL), a business language where queries, locking and transactions are part of the syntax. That pairing is why so many mid-market ERP, distribution and vertical ISV products were built on it, and why they still run on it decades later. The database offers replication, table partitioning, transparent data encryption, CDC and a SQL-92 engine for ODBC/JDBC reporting, while PASOE serves ABL logic over REST. 12.8 is the long-term-support line; 13.0 (February 2026) is a shorter-lived innovation release with ABL generics, a built-in AI coding assistant and FIPS 140-3 work.

pricing.notes: Licensed per user or core, often embedded in ISV application pricing; free time-limited trial.

scale.notes: Vertical scale with table partitioning; OpenEdge Replication for hot standby and DR.

strengths: ABL makes transactions, record locking and queries first-class language constructs
Very stable, long-lived databases that run with modest DBA effort
Built-in replication, partitioning, TDE and CDC options
Large catalogue of ERP and vertical ISV applications already built on it
weaknesses: ABL skills are scarce and the talent pool is ageing
SQL engine is secondary; complex reporting via ODBC can be slow
Proprietary stack ties applications to Progress licensing
useCases: Running ERP, distribution and manufacturing packages built on OpenEdge
Modernising ABL apps behind REST APIs with PASOE
ISV vertical applications sold to SMBs
notIdealFor: New applications outside the ABL ecosystem
Teams that need a large hiring pool
